strings.title: PIVOT_PLAN
strings.subtitle: Skill: long table to wide (pivot)
strings.briefing:
Store revenue arrives as one row per store per month. The report needs the opposite: one row per store with a column for each month.

Pivot the table so each store appears once, with columns store, jan, feb and mar. The month and revenue columns go away. Every total must be preserved.

In Python, put your reshaped table in df (df = ...), and that is what gets judged.

In SQL, create a NEW table named result that holds your answer: CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT ...; That table is what gets judged. You can run your query as often as you like; each run replaces the old result.
strings.task: Turn this long table into a wide one: one row per store, with the columns store, jan, feb and mar holding the revenue. The month and revenue columns must disappear and no total may change.

starterCode.python:
# df is long: 30 rows, columns store, month, revenue.
df.head(9)

python: The store becomes the row, the month becomes the columns, revenue fills the cells.
sql: SQLite has no pivot. Use conditional aggregation: one SUM(CASE WHEN ...) per output column, grouped by store.
SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'jan' THEN revenue END) AS jan

CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT store, SUM(CASE WHEN month='jan' THEN revenue END) AS jan, SUM(CASE WHEN month='feb' THEN revenue END) AS feb, SUM(CASE WHEN month='mar' THEN revenue END) AS mar FROM data GROUP BY store;
